subject: Discovery Recap — CareBridge private deployment & air-gap concerns
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Morris <alicia.morris@carebridge.health>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap — CareBridge private deployment & air-gap concerns

Hi Alicia / Peter (cc’d internally),

Thanks for taking the time today — appreciate the clear overview of CareBridge’s constraints. Below is a concise recap so we’re aligned and to surface the next steps from both sides. Please correct me if I missed anything.

1) Primary pain points and drivers
- Production latency variability and unexpected token-cost spikes on your current hosted inference provider.
- Regulatory requirement to keep PHI on-prem and strict E2E controls for key management.
- Need for deterministic maintenance windows for upgrades (air-gapped regime for some clinics).

2) Current stack (what you described)
- Inference runs in a hybrid setup: core EMR in on-prem datacenter, some analytics in AWS us-west-2.
- Model artifacts stored in internal artifact repo; currently no KMS integration for model-serving keys.
- Network: strict outbound whitelisting; only approved egress via a proxy; JIT connectivity windows for vendor updates.

3) Success criteria (pilot)
- Private deployment (VPC or on-prem container) that keeps inference traffic inside CareBridge network.
- Customer-managed KMS/HSM integration for token encryption and model keys.
- Demonstrated latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for typical 512-token workloads.
- Maintenance/update path that supports air-gapped clusters with signed bundles.

4) Constraints & blockers
- No persistent outbound connections from the air-gapped zones; update bundles must be staged by IT.
- Legal will need a draft MOU covering data handling, retention, and incident response prior to pilot.
- Procurement requires a list of third‑party subprocessors and an estimated spend profile for Q3 pilot.

5) Agreed next steps (action owners & tentative dates)
- Redwood: provide two architecture options (VPC w/ private link + KMS vs on‑prem container with HSM) — due Thu 2026-06-24 (Jordan / Marcus).
- CareBridge: share sanitized network diagram and list of approved egress/proxy endpoints — due Wed 2026-06-23 (Peter / IT).
- Legal/Procurement: CareBridge to identify legal contact for MOU redlines — target by 2026-06-25 (Alicia).
- Schedule technical deep-dive to walk through packaging and air-gap install process — propose Mon 2026-06-29 (all).

Attachments included with this email: carebridge-network-diagram.pdf (please send the version with firewall rules), redwood-dataplane-arch.png (high-level). I also attached an initial MOU template (mou-draft-carebridge.docx) for legal to review — it’s a first pass, so expect redlines.

If that aligns, I’ll lock the tech deep-dive time and circulate an agenda. Thanks again — excited to help CareBridge get a deployable, auditable inference stack in place.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192


From: Alicia Morris <alicia.morris@carebridge.health>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Peter Lang <peter.lang@carebridge.health>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 17:10:34 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap — CareBridge private deployment & air-gap concerns

Jordan,

Thank you — this is an excellent recap and mostly matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from the CareBridge side: 

- KMS: we must integrate with our on-prem HSM (Thales Luna). Any solution that requires keys to leave our environment is a non-starter.
- Air-gap updates: our clinics in Region West are fully air-gapped; updates must be delivered on signed tarballs and applied by our sysadmin during scheduled maintenance windows.
- Pilot scope: prefer starting with two clinics (one cloud-adjacent, one fully air-gapped) to validate both workflows.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Plus and HITRUST are on our procurement checklist; can you outline Redwood’s evidence matrix for SOC 2 controls and retention policies?

I’ll ask Peter to share the sanitized network diagram by EOD Tuesday. Legal: I will introduce our procurement lead (Meera Shah) to the thread once I have internal confirmation on the MOU cadence.

One minor ask — can Redwood confirm whether the on‑prem connector requires persistent outbound TLS or if we can operate in a store-and-forward pattern for control-plane messages? That determines if we can use a strictly offline install.

Alicia
Director, Clinical Platform | CareBridge Health
alicia.morris@carebridge.health | +1 312-555-0147

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap — CareBridge private deployment & air-gap concerns (Next steps & tech deep-dive)

Alicia / Peter —

Thanks for the quick replies and clarifications. Confirming next steps and including meeting logistics: 

- Tech deep-dive: Mon, 2026-06-29 at 10:00 AM PT — 45 minutes. Video link: https://meet.redwood.ai/s/tech-deep-dive-carebridge (I’ll send an invite).
- Deliverables before the deep-dive: 
  * Redwood to provide two architecture options + subprocessors list (Jordan / Marcus) — due 2026-06-24.
  * CareBridge to provide sanitized network diagram and list of approved egress endpoints (Peter) — due 2026-06-23.
  * Legal contact for MOU redlines (Alicia) — please introduce Meera when available.

- Regarding the on‑prem connector: short answer — we can support a store-and-forward control-plane model for air-gapped clusters. The control-plane can operate over a pull model where signed bundles are staged and applied by your sysadmin without persistent outbound TLS from the cluster. We’ll cover implementation details in the deep-dive.

Attached: mou-draft-carebridge.docx (first pass), redwood-dataplane-arch.png (option A sketch), carebridge-network-diagram.pdf (placeholder — please replace with your sanitized version).

Ask: please confirm availability for the deep-dive or propose two alternate windows. If Meera is available, it would be helpful to have procurement/legal on the call for a short (10 min) section on contract timeline.

Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192
